note.question: How should customer arrivals in service systems with multiple identical servers be managed?
note.overview: The paper analyzes a discrete multiserver model for scheduling customer arrivals under no-shows. The challenge is to assign customers to time slots so that the service system utilizes its resources efficiently and customers experience short waiting times. We provide theoretical and heuristic guidelines for an effective practice of appointment overbooking to offset no-shows.

Consider s identical service providers working in parallel.
Let I(x), O(x) and W(x) denote the expected servers’ total idle time, overtime, and customers’ aggregate waiting time, respectively, under schedule x.

The number of new arrivals at the beginning of each slot is a binomial random variable, not necessarily identically distributed, since we allow assignments of diﬀerent numbers of customers to diﬀerent slots.
